chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Gensel and the Eastern concert at St. Vincent's
summary: He recalls the packed concert that drew Reverend Gensel's attention.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I have another story about Basin Street East. I was with Duke, and I couldn't get... Duke was going into Basin

On 93rd Street. Then I didn't see him for a while. So the next time I saw him, I think it was up at Newport. I came back to New York, and I happened to run into him one day, and he was saying, "Let's put on the Eastern program." So I said, "Yeah, well, why not?" So wee decided to put it on down at 46th Street at the church there, what's the name of that church...? Oh, hell...

Yeah, it was St. Vincent's that we put on that Eastern concert, and the joint was loaded -- I mean, it was packed. So the Reverend from St. Peter's came over and saw all those people at the church. He went immediately to the High Reverend Gensel to bring him over there, and maybe bring all these people over there to the church, because St. Peter's wasn't doing too good.
This was '63 or '64, somewhere along there.
Around in the time that you had been refused the card at Basin Street East.
You kind of came out after being strung out and everything, and then you had a band with the organ player, Phil Porter. But that was in the early Sixties, wasn't it?
